newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens in range-trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens in range-trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said trading was slow and the rate was hovering in a three-point range, with sentiment remaining mixed.
"There is no clear trend yet. Sentiment is a bit mixed," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding that speculation of a steady liquidity at month-end helped the dollar rebound.
He said short-covering at month-end was probably the other reason which lifted the dollar back to its opening level.
Spot rupiah was at 2,426.25/26.65 at 0910 GMT after soaring to a high of 2,422.75 in the morning.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,425.75/26.25 and 2,423.6/24.0, respectively.
Dealers said fears over a possible rupiah tightening on Wednesday seemed to diminish after overnight money fell to 13.0/14.0 percent. It fluctuated throughout the day.
Overnight swap was at 0.50/0.55 and tom/next at 0.62/0.65.

The rupiah tumbled last week to a historic low of 2,440.5 on fears over possible violence during the campaign period lasting till May 23. But a smooth start to the campaign for May 29 general elections has helped calm the market.
However, one local bank dealer said the on-going campaign would limit further softening of the dollar.
"People tend to go long dollars for now. May be after the elections they would start unloading," he added.
The U.S. bank dealer said swap rates were little changed from the opening after trending up on early tight market.
One-month swaps were at 13.0/13.5, two at 25.0/26.0, three at 37.0/38.0 and six at 75.0/76.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,406/2,598 and the conversion band at 2,406/2,454 on Tuesday.
